content: Vaginal metronidazole is an antibiotic commonly used to treat bacterial vaginosis, an infection caused by specific bacteria. However, it is not effective against yeast infections, which may occur during or after treatment with vaginal metronidazole. If you experience symptoms of a yeast infection, such as vaginal discharge, itching, or discomfort, contact your healthcare provider. You may require treatment with an antifungal medication. Vaginal metronidazole can cause side effects, some of which may be serious. Common side effects include headache, vaginal itching, stomach pain, nausea, sore throat, rash, diarrhea, breast pain (with Vandazole), and painful or heavy menstrual periods. If any of these symptoms bother you, inform your healthcare provider. Serious side effects, though less common, include severe allergic reactions. Stop using vaginal metronidazole and seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms such as difficulty breathing, wheezing, a racing heart, fever, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing, throat tightness, hives, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, fainting, stomach cramps, or joint pain. Nervous system problems have been reported with other forms of metronidazole taken orally or by injection. Stop using vaginal metronidazole and contact your healthcare provider if you experience seizures, numbness, tingling, or pain in the hands or feet (peripheral neuropathy), confusion, difficulty thinking, or behavioral changes. Certain individuals should not use vaginal metronidazole. This includes those allergic to metronidazole, Vandazole, Nuvessa, parabens, nitroimidazole derivatives, or any ingredients in the specific product. Your pharmacist can provide a complete list of ingredients. Vaginal metronidazole may interact with other medications. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using. Avoid using vaginal metronidazole with medications such as warfarin (Coumadin), disulfiram (Antabuse) within the past two weeks, or lithium (Eskalith, Lithobid). Do not consume alcohol or foods containing propylene glycol while using vaginal metronidazole and for at least one day after stopping Nuvessa or three days after stopping Vandazole. Serious side effects may occur if alcohol is consumed during treatment. Before using vaginal metronidazole, inform your healthcare provider about your medical history, including any nervous system conditions like seizures or peripheral neuropathy. Discuss any medications or supplements you are taking to avoid potential interactions. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, consult your healthcare provider. It is not known how vaginal metronidazole may affect pregnancy or harm an unborn baby. Your provider will determine if it is safe for you to use during pregnancy. If you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, inform your healthcare provider. Vaginal metronidazole passes into breast milk. You may need to pump and discard your breast milk while using the medication and for two days after completing treatment. Vaginal metronidazole is for vaginal use only. Avoid sexual intercourse and the use of vaginal products like tampons or douches during treatment. If the medication comes into contact with your eyes, rinse them with cool water and contact your healthcare provider. Store vaginal metronidazole at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C). It can tolerate short-term exposure to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C), such as during transport. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use double or extra doses. Complete the full course of treatment as prescribed, even if your symptoms improve, to reduce the risk of developing antibiotic resistance. In case of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Vaginal metronidazole is available as a 0.75% vaginal gel under brand names such as Nuvessa and Vandazole, as well as in generic forms. It works by damaging the DNA of certain bacteria, effectively killing them. It may also be used for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider.
